title: Spouse Amount Included When a Suspended Disability Compensation Award Is Released
content:
In a Disability Compensation resumption release, the spouse addition is the spouse addition plus the spouse aid-and-attendance addition when a spouse is recorded on the award and the most recent spouse addition is marked as needing aid and attendance; the spouse addition alone when a spouse is recorded and the most recent spouse addition is not so marked; and nothing when no spouse is recorded. It is part of the monthly amount for every month the release covers.

A spouse is recorded when the spouse additions on the award exceed its spouse removals; the most recent spouse addition is the one with the latest effective date. The amounts are taken from the award's own tier.

**Cases (hypothetical award at Disability Compensation (80% Combined Rating))**

- Spouse recorded, most recent addition marked as needing aid and attendance: 176.24 plus 161.13, that is 337.37 a month.
- Spouse recorded, not so marked: 176.24 a month.
- Spouse added and then removed after a divorce: nothing.
